title: Unique lifts to a saturated fan blowup from sharp saturated spaces
statement:
Let $(T,\mathcal A)$ be a topological space with a sheaf of sharp saturated integral commutative monoids; integral means that every stalk embeds in its group completion, and saturated means that $nq$ in the stalk for $q$ in its group completion and $n>0$ implies $q$ in the stalk [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Let $F$ be a fine fan, $J\subset\mathcal P_F$ a nonempty coherent ideal, and $d:(T,\mathcal A)\to(F,\mathcal P_F)$ a continuous morphism with local stalk maps [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Suppose the ideal generated by $d^{-1}J$ in $\mathcal A$ is locally principal. Then there is a unique local morphism
$$\widetilde d:(T,\mathcal A)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}^{\mathrm{sat}}_J(F)$$
whose composite with the blowup map is $d$. Over an affine fan with sharp monoid $P$ and $J$ generated by a finite nonempty $E\subset P$, wherever the image of $a\in E$ generates the pulled-back ideal, this lift factors through the chart of $(\langle P,b-a\ (b\in E)\rangle)^{\mathrm{sat}}$ and its homomorphism on group completions extends the one induced by $P$. The unique lifts commute with restriction to open subsets of $T$ and with precomposition by morphisms of sharp saturated integral monoidal spaces. In particular any family of local lifts on an open cover agrees on overlaps and glues to this unique morphism.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.8, p.99; 3.1.19--3.1.25, pp.101--102; 3.3.13(i),(iii), pp.108--109: universal factorization and overlap gluing for saturated fan blowup charts.

proof.text: For every open $U\subseteq T$, the monoid $B=\Gamma(U,\mathcal A)$ is sharp and integral: a unit has zero germ everywhere, and cancellation holds on germs and hence on sections. It is saturated in $B^{\mathrm{gp}}$: if $g=s-t\in B^{\mathrm{gp}}$ and $ng\in B$, saturation at each stalk gives $g_x\in\mathcal A_x$, represented near $x$ by $r_x$. Equality $r_x+t=s$ in the stalk can be enforced after shrinking. On intersections these representatives agree by cancellation, so the sheaf axiom glues them to $r\in B$ with $r+t=s$. Thus $g\in B$. These observations use no finiteness hypothesis on $T$ or $\mathcal A$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.6, 3.1.8(ii), 3.1.17; elementary sectionwise consequence of the stalk hypotheses

proof.text: Every $z\in F$ has smallest open neighborhood $F_z\cong S(P)$ with $P=\mathcal P_{F,z}$ fine sharp and $\Gamma(F_z,\mathcal P_F)=P$ [lem-trf-fine-fan-point-localization]; as $F_z$ lies in any open where $J$ is finitely generated, $J|_{F_z}$ is generated by a finite nonempty $E\subset P$. Work over such a chart and write $h:P\to\Gamma(d^{-1}S(P),\mathcal A)$ for its section map. At $x$, let $t$ generate the pulled-back ideal. Since $t$ belongs to that ideal, $t=h(a)+u$ for some $a\in E$ and $u\in\mathcal A_x$; also $h(a)=t+v$. Cancellation gives $u+v=0$, hence $u=v=0$ by sharpness. For each $b\in E$, write $h(b)=h(a)+r_b$ in the stalk. Represent the finitely many $r_b$ and these equalities on a common neighborhood $U$ of $x$. Thus $h(a)$ generates the ideal on $U$. Such neighborhoods cover $T$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.18--3.1.19, 3.1.24; choosing a generator among the finite chart generators

proof.text: On such $U$, set $B=\Gamma(U,\mathcal A)$ and extend $h$ to $h^{\mathrm{gp}}:P^{\mathrm{gp}}\to B^{\mathrm{gp}}$ using the defining group-completion relations. The elements $b-a$ map to $r_b\in B$. Therefore $h^{\mathrm{gp}}$ maps $Q_a=\langle P,b-a\ (b\in E)\rangle$ into $B$. If $q\in C_a=Q_a^{\mathrm{sat}}$, choose $n>0$ with $nq\in Q_a$; then $n h^{\mathrm{gp}}(q)\in B$, so step 1 puts $h^{\mathrm{gp}}(q)$ in $B$. Restriction gives a homomorphism $k_a:C_a\to B$. It is the unique extension of $h$: since $P\subseteq Q_a\subseteq C_a\subseteq P^{\mathrm{gp}}$, all three group completions identify with $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$, so any extension has group map $h^{\mathrm{gp}}$.

The finite-saturation lemma applies to the finitely generated integral monoid $Q_a$, so $C_a$ is fine saturated. Its units form a face (if $u+v$ is invertible, both $u$ and $v$ are invertible). Apply the fs-face-sharpening lemma with this face to obtain a fine saturated sharp monoid $\overline C_a$. Since $B$ is sharp, $k_a$ kills units and factors uniquely through $\overline C_a$. The affine-fan Hom bijection now gives a unique local morphism $U\to S(\overline C_a)$ with this section map. The chart $S(\overline C_a)$ is the same sharp monoidal space as the specified chart $S(C_a)$: prime ideals correspond under the unit quotient, and localizing and then quotienting units gives the same monoids on basic opens, directly from the localization and quotient definitions. The composite to $S(P)$ has section map $h$; the Hom bijection identifies it with $d|_U$.

The $a$-chart of the blowup is exactly the locus where $a$ generates the pulled-back ideal. Indeed, on the $e$-chart the ideal is $e+\mathcal P$, since $b=e+(b-e)$ for all $b\in E$. At a stalk on that chart, $a$ also generates precisely when $a=e+w$ and $e=a+v$ for some $v$; cancellation says $w+v=0$, so $w=a-e$ is a unit. Conversely an invertible $a-e$ makes $a$ a generator. The unit locus of $a-e$ is $D(a-e)$ by the definition of the spectrum and local stalks. By the prescribed overlap gluing this is exactly the intersection with the $a$-chart. This argument includes $e=a$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19, 3.1.24--3.1.25; generator locus checked on every chart

proof.text: For any local lift $f$ over $F$, if $h(a)$ generates on $U$ then $f(U)$ lies in the $a$-chart: at $x$, choose an $e$-chart containing $f(x)$. The image of $e$ also generates the ideal at $x$, so sharpness and cancellation give $h(a)=h(e)$ there. Thus the chart element $a-e$ maps to a unit. Locality of the stalk map forces $a-e$ itself to be a unit at $f(x)$; step 5 puts $f(x)$ in the $a$-chart. On this open chart, its section map $C_a\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal A)$ extends $h$, so step 3 forces it to be $k_a$. The affine-fan Hom bijection then forces $f|_U$ to equal the lift constructed in step 4. This proves local uniqueness, including the asserted factorization wherever $a$ generates and the group-completion extension formula. It applies on an arbitrary such open, not just the neighborhoods chosen in step 2.

source.place: VIII 3.1.8(ii), 3.1.19--3.1.21, 3.1.24; local uniqueness including chart membership

proof.text: Two constructed lifts agree on every overlap by step 6, applied after covering its image in $F$ by affine charts and its source by principal-generator neighborhoods. They therefore glue: their continuous maps define one map, continuous because continuity can be checked on an open cover; on an open of the target the compatible homomorphisms into $\mathcal A$ glue by its sheaf axiom. The resulting stalk maps are the given local maps, hence local. This constructs $\widetilde d$ globally over $F$. Any other lift agrees with it on the neighborhoods of step 2 by step 6, hence agrees globally on both its underlying map and sheaf homomorphism.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19--3.1.25; explicit open gluing, also used in VIII 3.3.13(i),(iii)

proof.text: Restriction of a lift is a local lift of the restricted map, so uniqueness identifies it with the constructed lift. For a local morphism $g:(T',\mathcal A')\to(T,\mathcal A)$ between sharp saturated integral monoidal spaces, a local generator $s$ of the pulled-back ideal maps to a generator $g^\#s$ of the ideal for $d\circ g$: every generator relation maps to the corresponding relation, and $s$ itself is locally in the ideal generated by $d^{-1}J$. Thus the hypothesis holds for $d\circ g$, and $\widetilde d\circ g$ is a lift of it; uniqueness gives its prescribed lift. In particular any family of local lifts agrees on overlaps by uniqueness and glues as in step 7. For empty $T$ the unique empty map and its unique sheaf map give the same assertions.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19--3.1.22, 3.1.24--3.1.25; naturality from the proved uniqueness

proof_origin.place: VIII 3.1.8(ii), 3.1.17--3.1.25, pp.99--102; explicit extension of the fraction-chart proof to arbitrary sharp saturated integral monoidal spaces; VIII 3.3.13(i),(iii), pp.108--109
